questions.q: Where, exactly, does the fix for this discrepancy get applied?
options: In dw.FactProductSales directly, via an ALTER TABLE statement
Only in Finance's SUMIFS formula in the Excel workbook — changing the upper bound from <= to <
In both the Power BI model and the Tableau workbook simultaneously
In Chapter 3's Python validation script
questions.explain: The bug only ever existed in Finance's SUMIFS formula, so that's the only place the fix is applied.

questions.q: Why are the warehouse, Power BI, and Tableau all left untouched during this fix?
options: Because they are harder to edit than Excel
Because each is a read-only consumer and was never the source of the bug — the warehouse already used correct half-open logic, and Power BI/Tableau inherited that correctness
Because Finance does not have permission to request changes to them
Because changing them would violate Tableau Public's licensing terms
questions.explain: Nothing about the warehouse's date logic or the two other front-ends was ever wrong, so the fix stays scoped to the one deliverable that actually had the bug.

questions.q: What is the real bar for confirming this fix actually worked?
options: The three totals should be approximately close, within a reasonable margin
All three totals — Power BI, Tableau, and the corrected Excel formula — must match exactly, with zero remaining gap
Only Power BI and Excel need to match; Tableau is optional
The fix is confirmed as soon as the formula no longer shows an error
questions.explain: Since this was a boundary logic error, a correct fix should close the gap completely — any remaining difference, however small, means the fix isn't finished.

questions.q: Why does this lesson emphasize documenting the fix, not just applying it?
options: Documentation is only a formality with no real purpose
A number that silently changed is almost as risky as a number that was silently wrong — anyone who saw the old total needs to know why the new one differs
Excel requires a change log before any formula can be edited
Documentation replaces the need for the three-way re-validation
questions.explain: Recording what was wrong, when it was found, and what changed prevents confusion for anyone who previously saw the old, incorrect total.

questions.q: If Finance had built one SUMIFS formula per quarter per territory, what would the fix in this lesson require?
options: Only the original Q3 company-wide formula needs correcting
Every formula following the same inclusive-upper-bound pattern needs the identical correction — the exclusive upper bound, not just one instance of it
Rebuilding the entire workbook from scratch
Switching from SUMIFS to a PivotTable entirely
questions.explain: The same structural mistake would exist anywhere the same inclusive-boundary pattern was used, so every instance needs the identical fix.
